public_sources.title: Time-sensitive anytime-valid testing
public_sources.authors: Eugenio Clerico; Tobias Wegel; Iskander Azangulov; Patrick Rebeschini
public_sources.used_scope: Hard-deadline anytime-valid testing is a finite-horizon control problem; in the simple-vs-simple case the paper gives a Bellman/finite-horizon Neyman-Pearson characterization and shows that the optimal bet may depend on time and wealth. Used to justify the map-specific Bellman policies, not to claim the paper solved the present composite fixed-latent problem.

public_sources.title: Non-Rectangular Average-Reward Robust MDPs: Optimal Policies and Their Transient Values
public_sources.used_scope: Conceptual support for distinguishing a stationary adversary that commits to one model for the horizon from rectangular stage-wise nature, and for allowing history-dependent adaptation under fixed-model ambiguity. Its theorem is for average-reward robust MDPs, not this finite-horizon e-process.

public_sources.title: Policy Gradient Algorithms for Robust MDPs with Nonrectangular Uncertainty Sets
public_sources.authors: Mengmeng Li; Daniel Kuhn; Tobias Sutter
public_sources.used_scope: Nonrectangular uncertainty can better preserve statistically natural coupling but loses standard robust dynamic-programming tractability. Used only as structural background for why rectangularization may be conservative and why exact nonrectangular optimization can be harder.

public_sources.title: Partially Identified Ambiguity
public_sources.author: Cheaheon Lim
public_sources.used_scope: Distinguishes ex-ante Gamma-minimax and conditional Gamma-minimax under multiple priors and analyzes time-consistency issues. Used to keep ex-ante fixed-latent maximin distinct from stepwise conditional/rectangular re-optimization.

model_and_numerical_setup.null_and_e_factor: For pre-outcome stratum z in {low,high}, X=+1 candidate-only success, -1 incumbent-only success, 0 concordance. Any predictable b in [0,1] uses e=1+bX. Threshold is 20 (alpha=.05). Conditional sign-null validity is unchanged by the alternative-design calculations below.
model_and_numerical_setup.rectangular_baseline: Nature is allowed to use the marginal worst q=.60 in both strata, producing the unattested cross-context combination (.60,.60). A hard-deadline Bellman policy is designed for that rectangular worst case.
model_and_numerical_setup.structured_policy_search: For a prespecified design pair (q_design_low,q_design_high), solve the hard-deadline Bellman recursion over time and e-wealth for predictable affine bets, then evaluate that same policy under each of the three fixed maps. Grid searches over design pairs were used for T=100 and T=200; T=20/T=50 use the inverted-map Bellman policy.
model_and_numerical_setup.numerical_scope: Results are worker-local numerical calculations with finite wealth/action grids. They are not external empirical evidence and are not claimed as exact continuous-state optima.

fixed_latent_upper_bound_and_saddle_chec.derivation: Because the inverted map is in the ambiguity set, every policy satisfies min_m Power_m(policy) <= Power_inverted(policy) <= V*_inverted(T), where V*_inverted is the map-specific hard-deadline optimum. Therefore any policy whose power under all three maps is at least V*_inverted numerically attains the maximin upper bound for the discretized problem.
fixed_latent_upper_bound_and_saddle_chec.interpretation: At T=20 and T=50, the inverted-map-optimal Bellman policy also does better under the other two maps, so the discretized fixed-latent game has a numerical saddle at the inverted map; the least-favorable state can be degenerate rather than a diffuse prior.

near_minimax_longer_horizons.interpretation: The simple inverted-optimal policy ceases to be a saddle by T=100 because its power under the correct map can fall below its inverted-map power. Nevertheless a nearby time/wealth-aware design pair nearly saturates the universal inverted-map upper bound, leaving only a 0.0145 percentage-point numerical gap at T=100 and 0.106 percentage point at T=200 within the searched family/grid.

rectangularization_cost_in_reject_by_dea.interpretation: When the actual uncertainty is one fixed cross-stratum transfer map, allowing nature to independently combine marginal worst cases at every stratum can materially understate finite-horizon resolution. The effect is largest around intermediate horizons in this example, not monotone in T.
rectangularization_cost_in_reject_by_dea.scope_guard: This is not an argument to reject rectangularity generally. If the environment can actually change each stratum independently, the rectangular model is the correct threat model.

maximin_power_versus_minimax_regret.measurement_rule: Do not report a policy as generically 'robust' without naming the loss: maximizing worst-case probability of resolving by the deadline and minimizing regret relative to each environment's oracle policy select materially different bets.

null_implementation_sanity.description: 150,000 fair-sign trajectories per horizon, using the selected structured hard-deadline policies; empirical threshold-crossing is an implementation check only because validity follows from predictable affine e-factors.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: When transfer uncertainty is a fixed latent cross-context map, preserve that coupling in the finite-horizon objective instead of rectangularizing marginal q-ranges. Use map-specific hard-deadline Bellman policies plus a least-favorable-model upper bound to certify or bracket maximin performance; use belief-state/least-favorable-prior optimization only when the simple saddle check fails.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: In the two-stratum three-map worker-local problem, T=20 and T=50 exactly hit the inverted-map upper bound on the discretized grid. At T=100/T=200 searched time-sensitive design pairs came within 0.0145/0.106 percentage point of the same universal upper bound while improving worst-case deadline resolution over the rectangular baseline by 11.56/8.68 points.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Depends on the fixed-map threat model, known stratum frequencies/discordance rates, the three-map support, alpha=.05, and numerical Bellman/search discretization. A changing environment can make rectangularity appropriate.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Treat maximin deadline power, minimax regret, harmful-commit risk and unresolved cost as separate optimization objectives and meta-evaluate each policy under the objective actually used for deployment.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: At T=50 the searched maximin policy had worst power .4087 but max regret .2990, while the searched minimax-regret policy reduced max regret to .0622 yet lowered worst power to .3481. T=100 showed the same qualitative divergence.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: The regret calculation used map-specific Bellman optima and a restricted design-pair policy family; adding randomized/history-belief policies can move the frontier.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.update: Strengthened from long-run GROW-only evidence to hard-deadline control. Rectangularization cost is now directly visible in reject-by-deadline probability across T=20,50,100,200, with about 20% relative loss at T=50 and T=100 in the tested setup.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'rectangularizing a structured transfer-map uncertainty set is only a harmless conservative implementation detail.' It changed worst-case reject-by-deadline by 6.87 to 11.56 percentage points at T=50/T=100 in the tested problem.
Rejected: 'least-favorable priors must mix several environments.' At T=20/T=50 a degenerate inverted-map state numerically certifies the maximin value on the discretized Bellman problem.

Rejected: 'the optimal policy for the individually hardest map is always maximin for a fixed latent set.' By T=100 the inverted-optimal policy had lower power under the correct map than under inverted, so the simple saddle check fails even though a nearby design remains almost maximin.
Rejected: 'minimax power and minimax regret are interchangeable robustness criteria.' They chose sharply different finite-horizon bets and power profiles.

Narrowed: 'nonrectangular ambiguity always needs a full belief-state dynamic program.' It can, but a map-specific optimal-value upper bound plus cross-map policy evaluation can sometimes certify maximinity directly or leave a very small numerical optimality gap.

Narrowed: 'fixed-latent structure should always replace rectangular ambiguity.' Only when the model really commits to a fixed coupled environment; independent/adversarial per-stage changes justify rectangularity.

frontier.action: Solve the three-map fixed-latent hard-deadline problem with an explicit belief-state Bayes dynamic program and outer least-favorable-prior search at T=100/T=200. Verify the saddle/equalizer conditions and determine whether history-driven learning about the latent map improves on the near-minimax static design-pair policies.

Add at least one harmful/non-improving map with q<=.5 and explicit asymmetric harmful-commit plus unresolved costs. Compare maximin deadline power, Gamma-minimax regret and Bayes/least-favorable-prior policies under the same anytime-valid null constraint.

Stress fixed-latent policies when the map support is misspecified, when the latent map can switch once, and when stratum frequencies/discordance rates drift. Quantify the point at which rectangular or partially rectangular ambiguity becomes preferable.

Generalize the filtration-provenance gate to real evaluation traces: machine-check which task metadata, judge features, retrieval/tool outcomes, latency and retry indicators existed before the paired label whose bet they control.

Move reused-development candidate selection to actual anytime PACE paths and then add repeated-candidate run-level multiplicity, keeping candidate-generation selection validity distinct from within-candidate optional stopping.

frontier.exact_next_action: Implement a high-resolution three-map belief-state Bellman solver for the fixed-latent T=100/T=200 game, minimize Bayes-optimal deadline power over the prior simplex to obtain a numerical least-favorable prior, and check whether its Bayes policy equalizes the binding map powers and closes the remaining 0.0145/0.106 percentage-point upper-bound gaps before adding harmful maps.
